experiment.name: agentic-vs-singleshot
experiment.question: For the resume decision, does an agentic tool-loop beat a single-shot structured call on decision quality — and at what latency/reliability/token cost?
experiment.metric: qa-bench decision quality (grade.ts PASS-rate, 11 cases, shared qa_answer so planner-side carries the signal)
experiment.threshold_rule: Agentic wins (=> move architecture agentic) ONLY if quality >= +1 case (~+9pp) AND latency <= 2x baseline. Else single-shot wins.

verdict.rationale: Agentic tool-loop did NOT improve decision quality (9.67/11 vs single-shot 10.0/11 — flat-to-slightly-worse, both fail only the known noise cases C2a/C7/C9) while costing 3.65x latency (4717ms vs 1293ms) and ~5x tokens (~6955 vs one call) at 4.5 round-trips. Fails the pre-registered threshold (needed +1 case AND <=2x latency) on both axes. The task's inputs are small and fully known up front, so there is nothing for the agent to 'discover' via tools — the round-trips are pure overhead. SHIP single-shot (Approach A/B: deterministic spine + single structured decision). The more-agentic direction (C/D) is not justified by data on this task. The separate 'who hosts the loop' axis (our code vs Agora-native MCP) is moot here since the mechanism itself adds no quality; revisit only if a future task needs multi-step tool reasoning a single call cannot express.
